title: Andrew (30 November)
hookLine: the first called, who brought his brother Peter; patron of Scotland and of Constantinople

cards: "Come and see." That's the whole invitation. Two men have been standing with John the Baptist when Jesus walks past, and John points him out.
The two men leave John and walk after Jesus, saying nothing yet. Jesus turns and asks what they're looking for. They answer with a question: where do you live?
He says, come and see. They spend the rest of the day with him. One of those two men is named in the next verse: Andrew.

teach.h: ANDREW, THE BROTHER OF SIMON PETER.
teach.b: Look at how John's gospel introduces him. Not as Andrew, the disciple, but as "Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter." Even on his big day, he's somebody's brother.
And what does he do after his afternoon with Jesus? He goes home.
In the Douay-Rheims: "He findeth first his brother Simon, and saith to him: We have found the Messias." Then the verse ends simply: "And he brought him to Jesus."
That's Andrew's pattern, and John's gospel shows it more than once.

teach.h: A BOY WITH LOAVES, SOME GREEKS.
teach.b: When a huge crowd is hungry, Andrew points out a boy with five barley loaves and two fishes, even while wondering out loud what good so little could do.
When some Greeks come looking for Jesus, they ask Philip, and Philip goes to Andrew, and the two of them bring the request to Jesus. Peter gives the big speeches. Andrew makes introductions.

Eastern Christians call him the First-Called. Tradition says he preached around the Black Sea and was crucified on an X-shaped cross, which is why Scotland, which claims him as patron, flies a white X on blue.
The church of Constantinople honors him as its founder, the way Rome honors his brother Peter.

teach.h: AND HE BROUGHT HIM TO JESUS.
teach.b: In recent times, on Andrew's feast, a delegation from Rome visits the patriarch in Istanbul, and on Peter's feast a delegation from the patriarch visits Rome. The brothers are still bringing people to each other.

how: The feast of Saint Andrew, apostle, is kept on 30 November; it is a great feast in Scotland and for the church of Constantinople, and the season of Advent begins close to it.

o: Peter's brother, the first one Jesus called
a fisherman who denied Jesus three times
the disciple Jesus loved, who wrote a Gospel

p: Jesus's answer to where do you live

s: the other way round: Andrew found his brother and brought him to Jesus.
Andrew is the one who noticed the boy with the loaves
in John's gospel, before the crowd is fed.
Scotland's white X on blue recalls Andrew's cross
tradition says he was crucified on an X-shaped cross.

games.q: you're Andrew. you've spent the afternoon with Jesus, and you think you've found the Messiah. what's the first thing you do?
o: keep it to yourself for now
go back and report to John the Baptist
games.why: he findeth first his brother Simon. the gospel's next words: and he brought him to Jesus.

practice: Think of two people you know who don't know each other, but should: maybe they share a worry, a hobby or a hard season. Hold both faces in mind, and picture them meeting, and what they might give each other.
If you pray, bring both of them to God by name, the way Andrew brought his brother; if you don't, simply hold them both with care.

wordCard.voice: Andrew. Simon Peter's brother, called the First-Called, who spent one afternoon with Jesus and then went straight home to get his brother.

orig.note: Greek: the First-Called, the title Eastern Christians give Andrew.

carryVoice: Your line: he brought his brother. One afternoon with Jesus, and he went straight home. Same time tomorrow.
